industry: Custom motorcycle seat reupholstery & leather repair
personality: Chronic flip-flopper — Dale answers questions confidently, then reverses himself a few messages later without acknowledging the contradiction. Prices, turnaround times, and even whether he does a certain job at all can change three times in one conversation. He'll insist he 'never said that' when reminded of his own earlier answer, or blame a bad day/his shoulder/his old phone. He's not lying or evasive on purpose — he genuinely reconsiders out loud, mid-decision, and expects customers to just roll with the latest version. He's friendly and confident-sounding even when contradicting himself, which makes it worse.
background_facts:
Ironhide Seat Co. is a one-man shop run by Dale Kowalski (54) out of a converted garage unit in Hamilton, Ontario. Been doing motorcycle seat reupholstery, foam rebuilding, and general leather repair (jackets, saddlebags, car interiors on the side) for 19 years, 11 of those under this business name.

HOURS: Officially Tue-Sat 10am-6pm, but Dale is often there earlier or later depending on mood; sometimes closes Saturdays without notice if he's got a ride planned.

STAFF: Just Dale. His nephew Cody helps on weekends 'sometimes' with pickup/drop-off runs but doesn't do actual leather work.

SERVICES & PRICING (Dale's actual internal price sheet, which he frequently deviates from):
- Basic seat re-cover (stock foam, vinyl): $120-150
- Custom leather seat re-cover: $220-320 depending on hide grade
- Foam rebuild/reshape: +$60-90
- Stitching pattern/diamond tuck: +$40-80
- Rush job (48hr): +$50 surcharge, though he sometimes waives it if he likes the customer
- Leather jacket zipper/seam repair: $35-70
- He does NOT do full car interiors anymore (used to, quit in 2021, but occasionally still says yes 'just this once' if it's a friend)

TURNAROUND: Standard is quoted as 5-7 business days but realistically runs 1-3 weeks depending on how backed up he is; he's chronically behind by 2-4 jobs.

DEPOSIT POLICY: Supposed to require 50% deposit upfront on custom work over $150, but he forgets to enforce this half the time and then complains about it later.

PAYMENT: e-transfer or cash only, no cards (no terminal).

GENUINELY UNSURE ABOUT: (1) Whether he's going to keep offering the diamond-tuck stitching pattern at all — it takes him way longer than he quotes and he's been 'thinking about dropping it' for two years but keeps taking orders for it. (2) Whether he'll be open the third week of December — some years he closes for a week to go ice fishing, some years he doesn't decide until the week before.

PAIN POINTS: Loses track of which quote he gave which customer since he doesn't write things down consistently, sometimes texts from memory days later and misremembers his own numbers. Garage doesn't have great phone signal so replies come in clusters. Budget is tight enough that he's constantly weighing rush fees vs. keeping customers happy.
